label: 4th input token (t=3) when the first four tokens match a specific combination, mainly ..i followed by p/r
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely at t=3 (98% of mass; a few at t=2 and t=4), and never on the delimiter or copy phase. At t=3 it fires on only about 3% of steps, so it reads a conjunction of the first four tokens. Current token p, r, l, n, 3, y or c raises it (p and r most). Previous token i raises it most, then x, c, l, g. Two-back token (l, i, w, 2, d, h) and first token (h, k, d, w, v) add weaker contributions. The strongest activations are sequences like h w i r, h x i p, k e i p (first token h/k/d, i at t=2, p/r at t=3). It acts like a weighted sum over the tokens in a 4-token prefix, so a boolean token-set predicate tops out around F1 0.5. It does not fire on s, h, k or x as the current token, and only weakly on repeated tokens (in_first=0).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: p, r, l, n, y, 3; least: b, v, d, w) and the previous input (most: i, x, c, l, g, y; least: u, m, p, k); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=6 & t=3, L=8 & t=3.
